resources.name: Cloud Watching Dataset

resources.name: Orion Network Telescope
quotes: To obtain a diverse set of vantage points, we use existing honeypots from GreyNoise, deploy our own honeypots, and use the Orion Network Telescope.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The Orion Network Telescope is used as one of the primary vantage points for collecting scanning traffic, as described in Section 3.1.

resources.name: LZR
quotes: We use the open-source scanner LZR [45] to fingerprint unexpected services for 13 of the most popular TCP scanning protocols
references: [45] L. Izhikevich, R. Teixeira, and Z. Durumeric. LZR: Identifying unexpected Internet services. In USENIX Security Symposium, 2021.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors use LZR to fingerprint unexpected services on popular TCP scanning protocols in Section 6.

resources.name: Censys Universal Internet Dataset
quotes: IP addresses that previously hosted services that were indexed by Shodan [69] or Censys [32] attract a significantly different set of scanners
we investigate how attackers use the most-frequently scanning Internet service search engines [53]—Censys [32] and Shodan [69]—to find services.
references: [32] Z. Durumeric, D. Adrian, A. Mirian, M. Bailey, and J. A. Halderman. A search engine backed by Internet-wide scanning. In CCS, 2015.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors use Censys to identify previously indexed services to set up their 'leaked' honeypot experiment in Section 4.3.

resources.name: UMich|ZMap
quotes: Multiple motivations exist behind unsolicited network scans: organizations collecting datasets [32, 69], academic groups conducting research [35]
references: [35] Z. Durumeric, E. Wustrow, and J. A. Halderman. ZMap: Fast Internet-wide scanning and its security applications. In USENIX Security Symposium, 2013.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: ZMap is mentioned in Section 3.2 as an example of a tool used by academic groups for research, but it is not actively used in the paper's methodology.
